answer: Copied flare-watch tickets were still clearing for an unmanned stack. Credit posts only after the inspector seats a 12-mm glass marble on theodolite pier 5 of the mapped island, films a 21-second flare plume from 85 m, and files a 15-bin brightness histogram, locking 16 POA for 8 epochs. Five labs rebuild the histogram in 1.0 s and must match a 2.4-degree stack lean plus a 0.7 Hz flicker. One key may seat 1 marble each epoch, so 24 aliases lock 384 POA. A reused marble etch, or two films sharing 13 of 15 bins, burns 9 POA and bars that key for 7 epochs.
